Roofing in Grand Prairie, Texas

Grand Prairie runs from the I-30 corridor down to Joe Pool Lake, across three counties, and its Building Inspections Division wants a permit for any re-roof or roof repair. Call one free number any hour to reach a local roofing company.

Call (469) 649-7066 Grand Prairie re-roof rules
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. Grand Prairie

One city, three counties, one permit desk

Grand Prairie is long and narrow on the map. Most of it sits in Dallas County, a sizable slice lies in Tarrant County, and a small southern piece reaches into Ellis County, where part of Joe Pool Lake falls inside the city. The tax bill may come from different counties, but every roof job inside city limits answers to the same office: Grand Prairie Building Inspections.

That office is unusually plain about roofs. Its residential page says a permit is needed for any roof replacement, recover or repair. The contractor who files it must be registered with the city, and the application has to describe the work in detail and include the maker's specifications for the roofing going on.

DFW Expert Roofers does not file permits or work on roofs. Dial it and software, not a person, answers at whatever hour you call, notes your Grand Prairie address and the problem, and puts the call through to an independent, locally owned roofing company. The roofer you reach handles the rest directly with you.

Read the city's re-roof sheet like a bid checklist

Grand Prairie's re-roof guidelines list what a permit application must say. Ask every roofer you are comparing to put the same items in writing.

A real description of the work

The city's sample description runs through tearing off the existing shingles, checking for rot or damage, and replacing the underlayment, flashing, drip edge and vent boots. That is the level of detail a written quote should match.

Size and value

The application asks for square footage and the job's value. A bid that states the roof size in squares lets you compare one company's price against another's on the same footing.

The product, by name

Applicants attach the manufacturer's specifications for the roofing material. Ask which shingle line is on the quote, and whether its warranty will be registered in your name.

A registered contractor

The applicant needs a General Contractor registration with Grand Prairie and an account on the city's CSS portal. Ask for the company name on that registration and make sure it matches your contract.

Worn metal gets replaced

The guideline sheet repeats the code rule that existing flashings, edgings, outlets and vents that are rusted, damaged or deteriorated must be replaced, not reused. Ask how the roofer will judge yours.

Inspections to the 2021 code

The city inspects re-roofs to the 2021 International Residential Code. Ask who schedules the inspection, and keep the final payment until it has passed.

Tear off or lay over: the layer count decides

Grand Prairie quotes a code rule that ends many recover plans: no recover is allowed where the house already wears two or more applications of any kind of roof covering. Older homes that were re-roofed once by laying shingles over shingles are already at that limit.

What is on the roof nowWhat the city's sheet allowsAsk the roofer
One layer of shingles in fair shapeA recover may be possible if the deck and the existing layer meet codeWhy recover instead of tearing off, and what that does to the shingle warranty
Two or more layersNo recover; existing layers come off down to the deckHow many sheets of decking it expects to replace, and the price per sheet
Rusted or damaged flashing, edging or ventsThose parts must be replacedWhich metal parts are new on the quote, item by item

Questions about how your job fits these rules go to Building Inspections at 972-237-8230. The rules can change, so confirm with the city before signing.

The roofing jobs Grand Prairie callers ask about

Homes, apartment buildings and a large belt of warehouses and distribution centers share the city, so calls run from a single missing shingle to a torn membrane on a flat commercial roof.

Wind has peeled roofs here, too

Hail gets most of the attention in North Texas, but the two most recent tornadoes reported in Grand Prairie hit its industrial north end and its airport. On the night of March 16, 2023, the National Weather Service office in Fort Worth confirmed an EF-1 tornado that formed in the far northern part of the city, in a distribution facility area near West Trinity Boulevard and Trinity Ridge Drive. Surveyors found a section of roofing peeled off a warehouse there, then followed the tornado into Irving, where roof damage to an apartment building marked its peak winds, near 105 mph.

In January 2017 another confirmed tornado touched down near the Grand Prairie airport and ripped doors off a hangar. No one was hurt in either storm.

Lifted and creased shingles after a strong wind are easy to miss from the street, and a peeled membrane on a low-slope roof can let water in long before anyone sees it. If a storm has passed, look from the ground and from inside, never from the roof.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Before you hire a roofer in Grand Prairie

  • Ask for the company's Grand Prairie General Contractor registration and check it against the name on your contract.
  • Ask whether the job will be a recover or a tear-off, and how many layers are on the roof today.
  • Get the permit number before the old shingles come off.
  • Have the roofer's insurance agent email you its liability certificate directly.
  • Get the written scope to match the city's sample description, line by line.
  • If insurance is involved, let the adjuster see the damage first, and remember the deductible is yours.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

Lost shingles after a windstorm, a drip near the chimney, or a roof with too many layers already? Call and say so. A roofing company that serves Grand Prairie picks up, sizes up the roof on site and sets its own figure on paper.

Grand Prairie roofing questions

Does Grand Prairie require a permit for a roof repair, or only a full replacement?

Both. The City of Grand Prairie's residential re-roof page says a permit is required for any roof replacement, recovering or repair. The application goes through the city's online CSS portal and is usually processed in about 5 to 10 business days. Ask the roofer to show you the permit before work begins. The roof repair page covers what small repairs usually involve.

Who is allowed to pull a roofing permit in Grand Prairie?

A contractor registered with the city as a general contractor. Grand Prairie's General Contractor registration costs $75 and asks for company details, a signed application and a copy of the applicant's driver's license. Because Texas has no state roofing license, asking to see that city registration is a quick test of whether a roofer actually works in Grand Prairie. Building Inspections answers at 972-237-8230.

Can Grand Prairie roofers lay new shingles over the old ones?

Sometimes, but not if the house already carries two or more layers of roof covering. Grand Prairie's re-roof guideline sheet quotes the International Residential Code on this point, and the city inspects to the 2021 edition of that code. When a tear-off is required, the old layers come off down to the deck. Ask each bidder how many layers are on your roof now and which way they plan to go.

What should a roofing quote in Grand Prairie include?

Use the city's own permit example as a yardstick: tearing off the old shingles, checking the deck for rot or damage, new underlayment, flashing, drip edge and vent boots, and the shingle being installed, plus square footage and the job's value. A quote that only says "replace roof" leaves too much unsaid. Our DFW roof cost guide explains the price drivers.
